html:
The Mughal-Maratha Wars were twenty-seven years of fighting in the Deccan, from 1680 to 1707, between the emperor Aurangzeb and the Marathas. The Mughals won most of the sieges and lost the war. It broke the Mughal Empire.

Shivaji died in 1680. The next year Aurangzeb marched south with the whole court and an army of several hundred thousand. He never saw Delhi again.

At first he won. He conquered the sultanates of Bijapur in 1686 and Golconda in 1687. In 1689 he captured Shivaji's son Sambhaji and had him tortured to death. The Maratha king's brother fled to the fort of Gingee in the far south, which held out for eight years.

The Marathas then fought without a centre. Bands of light horse under leaders such as Santaji Ghorpade cut supply lines, raided deep into Mughal provinces and took back forts as soon as the imperial army moved on. From 1700 the widowed queen Tarabai led them.

Aurangzeb, in his eighties, went on besieging hill forts one at a time. He died in his camp in 1707. The treasury was empty and the north had been neglected for a generation. Within fifty years the Maratha Confederacy was the main power in India.
sum: The Mughal-Maratha Wars were twenty-seven years of fighting in the Deccan, from 1680 to 1707, between the emperor Aurangzeb and the Marathas. The Mughals won most of the sieges and lost the war. It broke the Mughal Empire.
